gaps: X_ITE 16.6.0 samples the texture surface with haveWeights false, so the weight field of a NurbsTextureCoordinate does nothing (the texture coordinates are the plain B-spline of the control points); the standard calls it rational; the bridge does what X_ITE does and the fixture asserts X_ITE's numbers
the tessellation of the texture surface is the surface's own (one grid): a texture surface is sampled at the same fractions of its own domain as the patch
scope: the 4 numbers X_ITE keeps per texture coordinate (x, y, 0, w) are compared by their first two; only the picture of the two patches on screen is compared as a picture (silhouette overlap, mean colour)
